about: For deck (studio experiments E02, E09, E13): the Agent Behaviour Policy model as worded on riskmandate.ai/abp.html and abp.sgit.ai (v0.12.1), the four barrier kinds from the raw data/barriers.json, and all five published examples with their grant rows drawn from the raw profile.json and delta.json files. The grant rows ARE published (every capability, its barrier kind, control text, undo class, evidence tier and tools), so blast radius can be drawn from rows. Not published / caveats: no example is measured on a real Claude Code install (0 of 22 rows measured; rows derived from architecture); mandates are the site's own first drafts, not elicited from deployers; both sites are one author's network, so no independent corroboration; data pack v0.8.0 retrieved 2026-09-11. Captures by researcher@the-ultimate-insider, 2026-10-29.

agent_behaviour_policy.definition: a written description, for one agent in one deployment, of everything it can do, what you authorised it to do, the gap between the two, and what actually stands in the way
agent_behaviour_policy.quote: An Agent Behaviour Policy is a written description, for one agent in one deployment, of everything it can do, what you authorised it to do, the gap between the two, and what actually stands in the way.

mandate.definition: What the agent is authorised and expected to do; elicited, in minutes, because you already know it
mandate.quote: The mandate What the agent is authorised and expected to do Elicited. In minutes, because you already know it

also.quote: The mandate What the agent is authorised and expected to do Elicited. In minutes, because the deployer already knows it

grant.definition: Everything the agent can do; measured, from the deployment shape, the account and the credentials
grant.quote: The grant Everything the agent can do Measured. From the deployment shape, the account and the credentials

also.quote: The grant Everything the agent can do Measured. From the deployment shape: the product, where it runs, with what account, with what credentials

delta.definition: Excess where it can and you did not ask; shortfall where you asked and it cannot. Derived, recomputed when grant or mandate moves, stored with both versions, never edited
delta.quote: The delta Excess where it can and you did not ask; shortfall where you asked and it cannot Derived. Recomputed whenever the grant or the mandate moves, stored with the versions of both, never edited

barrier.definition: What stands between the agent and each capability, recorded per capability from one of four kinds
barrier.quote: The barrier What stands between the agent and each capability Recorded per capability, from one of four kinds

excess.definition: a count of capabilities in the grant and not in the mandate
excess.quote: Excess is a count of capabilities in the grant and not in the mandate.

unbounded_excess.definition: how many of the excess capabilities sit at a barrier that is not a control
unbounded_excess.quote: Unbounded excess is how many of those sit at a barrier that is not a control.

shortfall.definition: Capabilities in the mandate and not in the grant
shortfall.quote: shortfall Capabilities in the mandate and not in the grant

enforcer_test.definition: A control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include.
enforcer_test.quote: A control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include.

also.quote: A control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include.

no_score_rule.definition: The ABP describes and does not judge; no rating, traffic light or risk level
no_score_rule.quote: So there is no rating on a behaviour policy, no traffic light and no risk level

capability_primitives.definition: capabilities are ids of the form verb.object.reach, 23 primitives in the grammar
capability_primitives.quote: The capability grammar verb.object.reach . 23 primitives, each with the undo class of its effect.

barrier_kinds.definition: a rule in prose, enforced by nobody
barrier_kinds.why: A rule in prose is inside the boundary the agent operates in. All four major model providers stated in their own 2026 words that an instruction at this layer can be bypassed.
barrier_kinds.quote: "published_meaning": "a rule in prose, enforced by nobody"

barrier_kinds.definition: a switch the agent's own account can flip
barrier_kinds.why: The grant includes the ability to remove the bound.
barrier_kinds.quote: "published_meaning": "a switch the agent's own account can flip"

barrier_kinds.definition: enforced above the grant, out of the agent's reach
barrier_kinds.why: Enforced by something the grant does not include. The only row that bounds anything.
barrier_kinds.quote: "published_meaning": "enforced above the grant, out of the agent's reach"

barrier_kinds_note: Order weakest first: none, expectation, setting, boundary. The four ids and meanings are the upstream pack's control_tiers; is_control and why are abp.sgit.ai's own reading, as barriers.json's provenance note says. A fifth glyph, 'absent' (dot), means 'not in this grant' and is not a barrier.

examples.name: A coding agent on your own machine, confirmations on
examples.agent: Claude Code (the CLI, on your own machine), variant local-default
examples.mandate_text: I want it to read and change the project I pointed it at, run the build and the tests, commit to that repository, and fetch the packages and docs it needs. I did not sign up for it reading the rest of my disk, my credentials or my shell history, sending anything to anyone, publishing under my name, changing its own permission settings, or leaving anything behind that runs after it stops.

rows.barrier: branch discipline in prose, if any
the tool's own directory restriction and its confirmation prompt, enforced by the tool, which runs inside the grant; anything that can execute as you steps around it
the settings file is owned by the same account

examples.quote: Grant 16 of 23 primitives Everything the agent can do Mandate 5 primitives What the deployer authorised and expected Excess 12
examples.note: 16 - 5 = 11 is the wrong sum: the mandate's 5 include send.endpoint.allowed, which is not in the grant (shortfall 1). Only 4 mandate items are granted (aligned), so excess = 16 - 4 = 12. Excess splits into 10 refused + 2 unstated (send.endpoint.world, write.repository.tenant). All 12 excess are unbounded. execute.process.host is in the mandate and sits at 'setting' (the confirmation prompt). Every row is DERIVED from what a CLI running as your account is, not measured on any instance ('Measured 0 of 22 rows': 22 is the count of tool-level rows, i.e. the 16 capabilities summed over the tools that reach them).

examples.agent: Claude Code (the CLI, on your own machine), variant local-confirmations-off
examples.mandate_text: I want it to read and change the project I pointed it at, run the build and the tests, commit to that repository, and fetch the packages and docs it needs. I did not sign up for it reading the rest of my disk, my credentials or my shell history, sending anything to anyone, publishing under my name, changing its own permission settings, or leaving anything behind that runs after it stops.

rows.barrier: none, confirmations disabled; the tool runs whatever it decides to run
branch discipline in prose, if any
the settings file is owned by the same account

examples.quote: Grant 16 of 23 primitives Everything the agent can do Mandate 5 primitives What the deployer authorised and expected Excess 12
examples.note: Same 16 rows as confirmations on; the only row that differs is execute.process.host, barrier setting -> none (control text: 'none, confirmations disabled'). It is inside the mandate, so no count moves. grant.credential.self stays at 'setting' in both. abp.sgit.ai records that its own foundation document predicted every delta barrier would move by one row; the data moves exactly one, and the site logs that as a disagreement. Mandate rows read from the shared mandate file (captured in abp-sgit-cc-on-data).

examples.agent: A generic browser extension with broad host permissions

examples.name: A CI job on a hosted runner, under a service account
examples.agent: GitHub Actions runner (a hosted CI job), variant ci
examples.settings: workflow permissions block, token contents:read, unrestricted egress
examples.mandate_text: Check out the code, build it, run the tests, fetch what it needs, and, when a release is cut, push the tag. I did not want it reading credentials beyond its own token.

rows.barrier: the checkout is writable, but the token is contents:read, so nothing written can leave

examples.quote: Grant 8 of 23 primitives Everything the agent can do Mandate 5 primitives
examples.note: Mandate 5 but only 4 granted (write.repository.tenant, pushing the tag, is the shortfall), so excess = 8 - 4 = 4 and 8 - 5 = 3 would be wrong. Unbounded excess 3, not 4: write.repository.project is excess but sits at 'boundary' (the token is contents:read), the only control in the five examples. All 4 excess are unstated by the mandate, none refused. The only example with measured rows: 8 of 8, measured 26 August inside the runner.

claims.note: Holds as a count of the published record (16 grant rows in profile.json, listed one by one). It is a derived model, not a measurement: 0 of 22 rows measured. As a claim about what Claude Code can do on a real machine it rests on one party's architectural reasoning (A2 at most).

evidence.quote: Mandate 5 5
It authorises 5 primitives, refuses 11 and says nothing either way about 7 .

claims.note: The mandate is a first draft written by the site, not elicited from a real deployer: 'authored 2026-09-09 by the site, as a starting point - not measured, not surveyed'. The 5 are read.file.project, write.file.project, execute.process.host, write.repository.project, send.endpoint.allowed.

evidence.quote: Excess 12 12
"aligned": 4
Shortfall: 1. Asked for and cannot: send.endpoint.allowed .

claims.note: The numbers add up, but not by 16 - 5. Excess is grant minus the mandate items actually granted: 16 - 4 aligned = 12. The fifth mandate item, send.endpoint.allowed (reach only the hosts it needs), is not in the grant; the grant has send.endpoint.world instead, which counts as excess. So mandate 5 = aligned 4 + shortfall 1. No row is 'in the mandate but over-granted' in the data; the over-grant shows up as a different capability id (world reach instead of allowed reach). A deck that draws 16 bars with 5 in the mandate must show 4 inside the grant and 1 outside it.
claims.suggested_wording: Grant 16, mandate 5 (4 of them granted, 1 it cannot do), excess 12

Every one of the 12 excess capabilities here is unbounded.

claims.note: No excess row sits at 'boundary': 10 at none, 1 at expectation (write.repository.tenant), 1 at setting (grant.credential.self).
